extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent practitioners (applicants/attorneys) preparing or evaluating 37 CFR 1.131/1.132 affidavits and declarations to antedate references or traverse rejections
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing, presenting, and examining affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 (antedating references) and 1.132 (traversing rejections), including evidentiary, formal, timing, geographic, and substantive sufficiency requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit may overcome rejection without identical disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit or declaration may be sufficient to overcome a rejection even if it does not show identical disclosure of the reference(s) relied upon, provided it contains facts showing completion of the invention commensurate with the extent of the invention as claimed in the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If affidavit shows a completion commensurate with the claimed invention, it is sufficient whether or not it is an identical disclosure of the reference (In re Wakefield).

rubrics_metrics.name: Must establish possession of the basic inventive concept
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit that relies on showing obvious variations must still establish possession of the invention (the basic inventive concept) and not merely of what one reference happens to show if that reference does not itself teach the basic inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even where differences between affidavit evidence and claimed invention would have been obvious, the affidavit must establish the inventor's possession of the inventive concept (In re Spiller example: affidavit established use of electrostatic forces as the basic invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Swearing behind combined references (plurality) — showing completion prior to effective date of any reference
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may overcome a 35 U.S.C. 103 rejection based on a combination of references by showing completion of the invention prior to the effective date of any of the references; applicant need not antedate the reference with the earliest filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 1.131 affidavit must show possession of either the whole invention as claimed or something falling within the claims prior to the effective date of the particular reference being antedated; it is not enough to show only what a reference happens to show if that reference lacks the basic inventive concept.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic claims: single species may antedate reference (general rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reference applied against generic claims may, in most cases, be antedated as to such claims by an affidavit or declaration under 37 CFR 1.131 showing completion of the invention of only a single species within the genus prior to the effective date of the reference (absent statutory bar or a patent claiming the same invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ex parte Biesecker and cases; practice differs in unpredictable arts (see MPEP § 715.03).

rubrics_metrics.name: Genus-species predictability test (unpredictable arts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where predictability is in question, the affidavit or declaration must show as much as the minimum disclosure required by a patent specification to furnish support for a generic claim; showing a single species may not ordinarily withdraw a rejection based on a reference disclosing a species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The test is whether species completed by applicant provide an adequate basis to infer that the invention has generic applicability; more species may be required for large/unpredictable genera (cases: In re Shokal, Mantell, Rainer, DeFano, Clarke).

rubrics_metrics.name: Species claim defeated by reference species — direct and indirect routes
rubrics_metrics.description: If the claimed subject matter is a species and the reference discloses that species, the rejection can be overcome directly by showing prior completion of the claimed species or indirectly by showing prior completion of a different species plus that the claimed species would have been an obvious modification of the species completed by applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See In re Spiller and other cited cases for examples of direct vs indirect overcoming.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference discloses multiple species of a genus — showing required
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference discloses several species of a claimed genus, the reference can be overcome directly under 37 CFR 1.131 only by a showing that the applicant completed, prior to the date of the reference, all of the species shown in the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, applicant may antedate indirectly by proving possession of one or more species which put applicant in possession of the claimed genus (test: adequacy of basis to infer generic applicability).

rubrics_metrics.name: Species versus embodiments distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: References disclosing one or more embodiments of a single claimed invention (as opposed to species of a claimed genus) can be overcome by filing a 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit showing prior completion of a single embodiment of the invention, whether the same or different from that in the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited cases (In re Fong, In re Defano) illustrate when reference disclosures are treated as embodiments rather than species of a genus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements of affidavits and declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit must be sworn before an authorized officer (notary, magistrate, etc.). A declaration under 37 CFR 1.68 may be used in place of an affidavit and must include an acknowledgment that willful false statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and statements that statements of personal knowledge are true and statements on information and belief are believed to be true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 604–604.06 for additional formal requirements; declarations must include the specified acknowledgements and language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may make affidavit or declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 must be made by (A) all inventors of the subject matter claimed; (B) fewer than all named inventors where it is shown that the signers are the inventors of the subject matter under rejection; or (C) the assignee or party in interest when it is not possible to produce the inventor's affidavit or declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where some named inventors are unavailable, signatures of remaining joint inventors are sufficient provided the affidavit shows completion by all joint inventors of the subject matter (see In re Carlson).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.131 ineffective to antedate identical or non-patentably-distinct US patents
rubrics_metrics.description: A 37 CFR 1.131 affidavit is ineffective to overcome a U.S. patent where there is verbatim correspondence between claims of the application and the patent, or where there is no patentable distinction between the respective claims (i.e., claiming the 'same patentable invention').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a domestic patent claims the same patentable invention and its issue date is within certain time windows relative to presentation of claims, other procedures (37 CFR 1.608, interference, or 35 U.S.C. 135(b)) may apply; see MPEP §§ 2306–2308 and forms for office action notation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facts, not conclusions — evidentiary specificity required
rubrics_metrics.description: The essential thing to be shown under 37 CFR 1.131 is priority of invention by satisfactory evidence of FACTS; mere conclusions or general allegations are insufficient. Each exhibit relied upon should be specifically referred to in the affidavit/declaration in terms of what it is relied upon to show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of acceptable exhibits: sketches, blueprints, photographs, notebook reproductions, models, supporting witness statements, interference testimony, disclosure documents. Vague general statements about exhibits amount to mere pleading and fail (In re Borkowski, Ex parte Saunders).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibits and compliance with 37 CFR 1.91
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits and models accompanying affidavits/declarations must comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into an application file; otherwise they may be disposed of or returned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ex parte Donovan: original exhibits or photocopies should accompany the affidavit or satisfactory explanation for their absence must be provided. When reviewing a 1.131 affidavit the examiner considers all evidence in its entirety; an exhibit need not support all limitations if the declaration itself supplies missing limitations (Ex parte Ovshinsky).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear explanation of what exhibits show
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration and exhibits must clearly explain which facts or data the applicant relies on to show completion prior to the reference date; vague or general descriptions are insufficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must point out exactly what facts are established and relied upon by applicant (In re Borkowski, In re Harry). If sketches/models were made and lost, reproduce and furnish in place of originals or explain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of dates and handling of redacted dates
rubrics_metrics.description: If dates on exhibits have been removed or blocked, dates can be established in the body of the oath/declaration. When alleging conception or reduction to practice prior to a reference, the oath/declaration may allege acts occurred prior to a specified date if the applicant does not want to disclose actual dates; however, actual dates of acts relied upon to establish diligence must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide actual dates where required for diligence; otherwise may allege occurrence prior to specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three ways to show prior invention under 37 CFR 1.131
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration must state facts and produce documentary evidence sufficient to show one of: (A) reduction to practice of the invention prior to the effective date of the reference; (B) conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to the reference date to a subsequent actual reduction to practice; or (C) conception prior to the effective date coupled with due diligence from prior to the reference date to the filing date of the application (constructive reduction to practice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conception alone is not enough unless followed by reasonable diligence to a reduction to practice or filing; filing constitutes constructive reduction to practice (37 CFR 1.131).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof standards for conception, reduction to practice, and utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Conception must be capable of proof (e.g., drawings, disclosure to another). Actual reduction to practice normally requires showing the apparatus existed and worked, though for very simple devices mere construction and demonstrative evidence may suffice. Proof of utility is required only if the reference discloses a utility; whether test results are needed depends on case facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroboration is not required for averments in a 1.131 affidavit/declaration (applicant may stand on own affidavit) though interference practice differs; ultimate issue is whether a person of ordinary skill would be reasonably certain of the possession and utility (In re Blake, In re Asahi/America).

rubrics_metrics.name: Diligence: need for factual showing and critical period
rubrics_metrics.description: When relying on conception prior to the reference date, applicant must show facts establishing diligence; diligence is judged over the critical period beginning just prior to the effective date of the reference and ending with the date of reduction to practice (actual or constructive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diligence must be shown by evidence of facts — mere allegations are insufficient. An inventor may be considered diligent even during periods of inactivity if inactivity is excused, but the record must set forth an explanation. Only diligence before reduction to practice matters; lapse between completion and filing is irrelevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts relied upon must occur in U.S. or NAFTA/WTO member country
rubrics_metrics.description: The affidavit/declaration must allege that the acts relied upon to establish the date prior to the reference were carried out in the United States or in a NAFTA or WTO member country; 35 U.S.C. 104 limits reliance on foreign acts except as provided by sections 119 and 365.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under 37 CFR 1.131(a) dates of completion in NAFTA/WTO member countries may be established only on/after the statutory effective dates (NAFTA: Dec 8, 1993; WTO for non-NAFTA: Jan 1, 1996). Acts before those dates may be relied upon but cannot be used to establish a date under 1.131 before those effective dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition and entry of exhibits
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibits filed with affidavits/declarations must comply with 37 CFR 1.91 to be entered into the application file; exhibits that do not comply may be disposed of or returned to applicant at the Office's discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.03(a) and § 715.07(d) for exhibit handling; examiner reviews exhibits when considering the affidavit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary examiner review and avenues for review
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of sufficiency of affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 should be reviewed and decided by the primary examiner; review of formal sufficiency/propriety is by petition to Group Directors; review on the merits is by appeal to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitions address formal issues; appeals address substantive sufficiency determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness (seasonable presentation) rules for 1.131 affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.131 are timely if submitted: (A) prior to a final rejection; (B) before appeal in an application not having a final rejection; or (C) after final rejection when submitted (1) with a first reply after final rejection to overcome a new ground of rejection or requirement made in the final rejection, (2) with a satisfactory showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) or 1.195, or (3) under 37 CFR 1.129(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All admitted affidavits/declarations are acknowledged and commented upon by the examiner in the next action. Refusal to enter an untimely affidavit is reviewable by petition, not appeal (In re Deters). For affidavits filed after appeal see 37 CFR 1.195 and MPEP § 1211.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review for prior public use, on-sale bar, and best mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must review affidavits/declarations and accompanying evidence to determine whether they show that the claimed invention was in public use or on sale in the U.S. more than one year prior to the effective filing date (statutory bars). Also, if the 1.131 evidence relies on an embodiment not disclosed in the application, the best mode requirement must be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if an affidavit overcomes a reference, prior public use or on-sale activities may create a statutory bar that cannot be overcome under 1.131 (see MPEP § 2133.03). A best mode rejection should be made only where the record, by a preponderance of the evidence, shows the specification fails to set forth the best mode contemplated by the inventor (see MPEP § 2165–2165.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.132 affidavits — traversing rejections and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits/declarations under 37 CFR 1.132 may be received to traverse rejections based on a U.S. patent which substantially shows but does not claim the same patentable invention, foreign patents, printed publications, facts within the personal knowledge of an Office employee, allegations about mode or capability of operation, inoperative or non-utility contentions, or objections that the alleged invention is frivolous or injurious to public health or morals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary examiner personally reviews whether a 1.132 submission is responsive to the rejection and presents sufficient facts to overcome it. The enumerated grounds in the rule are exemplary; affidavits falling outside other specific rules should be treated under 1.132. Use MPEP form paragraphs (7.65–7.66 and subparagraphs) when commenting on 1.132 affidavits.
